title: Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention
quote: Accordingly, vLLM sets its default block size as 16.
proves: Block-size ablation (Sec 7.2): small blocks underuse GPU parallelism, large blocks raise internal fragmentation and lower sharing probability; ShareGPT best at 16-128, Alpaca best at 16-32. Swap vs recompute (Sec 7.3): swapping has excessive overhead at small block sizes, recompute overhead is constant across block sizes and never above 20% of swap latency; comparable at block 16-64.
does_not_prove: Measured on 2023 kernels, A100-class GPUs, two traces, no prefix caching; the default 16 was never re-measured for later kernels (FlashAttention, FlashInfer), prefix-hit granularity, or unified memory. Swap measurement predates cross-layer contiguous layouts.
bearing: supports: block-size tradeoff gap (default 16 rests on 2023 data); supports: swap-vs-recompute crossover revisit

title: vAttention: Dynamic Memory Management for Serving LLMs without PagedAttention
quote: changing block size changes the execution time of the kernel by as much as 1.9×
proves: Paged prefill kernel up to 37% slower than non-paged (FA2), decode up to 12% slower; FlashInfer paged prefill up to 42% slower. vLLM paged decode is significantly worse at block 64/128; FA2 needed block 256 and smaller blocks raised its latency up to 9%. Block-table preparation contributed 30% of decode latency. Uses CUDA VMM with custom 64KB/128KB/256KB page groups; 2MB pages cause fragmentation; allocation overlapped with compute hides VMM latency.
does_not_prove: CUDA/NVIDIA only; kernel versions from 2024; does not measure prefix-hit granularity vs page size, nor unified-memory systems where there is no separate device VMM.
bearing: threatens: 'contiguous virtual KV is new' ideas; supports: kernel-speed vs block-size measurement on non-CUDA kernels

title: kvcached (ovg-project/kvcached) README
quote: Elastic KV cache: allocate and reclaim KV memory dynamically to match live load
proves: Engines reserve virtual memory only and back it with physical GPU pages on demand; default physical page 2 MiB, larger when a KV block or Mamba state slot exceeds 2 MiB; integrates with vLLM (>=0.17, tested to 0.30) and SGLang; self-reported 2-28x TTFT reduction with three Llama-3.1-8B on one A100-80G.
does_not_prove: Vendor/project benchmark only; multi-model sharing focus; CUDA VMM based, no Apple/MLX path; no independent study of page-size choice.
bearing: threatens: elastic KV pool on CUDA; supports: elastic pool on unified memory as distinct problem

title: Prism: Unleashing GPU Sharing for Cost-Efficient Multi-LLM Serving
quote: it supports on-demand memory allocation by dynamically mapping physical to virtual memory pages
proves: Dynamic virtual-to-physical page mapping lets multiple models space- and time-share a GPU; more than 2x cost savings and 3.3x SLO attainment vs state of the art.
does_not_prove: Multi-model GPU sharing, not single-model KV policy; abstract-level numbers only (OSDI'26 version seen only in search snippet).
bearing: threatens: elastic KV memory across models

title: vTensor: Flexible Virtual Tensor Management for Efficient LLM Serving
quote: due to the tightly coupled page management and computation kernels
proves: VMM-based virtual tensors decouple KV page management from kernels and do defragmentation outside compute; 1.86x average speedup, up to 2.42x in multi-turn chat, 2.12x/3.15x kernel speedups, frees ~71.25% (57GB) on A100 vs vLLM.
does_not_prove: Baseline is an older vLLM; CUDA VMM only; does not isolate how much gain is layout vs scheduling.
bearing: threatens: defragmentation/contiguous-KV ideas on CUDA

title: eLLM: Elastic Memory Management Framework for Efficient LLM Serving
quote: decouples the virtual address space of tensors from the physical GPU memory
proves: Unified pool across activations and KV with ballooning-style inflation/deflation, using host RAM as headroom; 2.32x higher decoding throughput and 3x larger batch sizes for 128K-token inputs.
does_not_prove: Discrete-GPU design where host RAM is a separate tier; on unified memory host RAM and GPU memory are the same pool, so the CPU-buffer mechanism has no direct analogue.
bearing: threatens: elastic activation/KV pool on CUDA; supports: unified-memory variant is unstudied

title: Jenga: Effective Memory Management for Serving LLM with Heterogeneity
quote: Jenga improves GPU memory utilization by up to 79.6%
proves: Two-level allocator using LCM of embedding sizes with per-layer caching/eviction logic for heterogeneous layers (sliding window, Mamba, etc.); up to 4.92x (1.80x average) throughput on vLLM.
does_not_prove: Abstract-level numbers; NVIDIA GPUs; whether vLLM's shipped hybrid manager matches Jenga's LCM design is not stated here.
bearing: threatens: new hybrid-model allocator; supports: measuring padding waste of shipped allocator

title: Hybrid KV Cache Manager (vLLM design doc)
quote: The solution has some memory waste and is not perfect.
proves: vLLM requires a single page size across all layer groups; for Mamba hybrids it raises attention block_size, which 'can lead to more than 400 block_size for attention layers'; sliding-window layers free out-of-window blocks; prefix cache hit for sliding window needs only last sliding_window_size-1 tokens; models with more than 2 attention types unsupported; padding strategy 'still a work in progress'.
does_not_prove: No measurement of padding waste or of the kernel cost of 400+ token blocks; heuristic explicitly provisional.
bearing: supports: measuring hybrid-allocator padding waste and block-size inflation (unmeasured)

title: vllm.config.cache (CacheConfig API docs)
quote: If unspecified, will use the default value of 0.92.
proves: Current knobs: block_size (DEFAULT_BLOCK_SIZE = 16), gpu_memory_utilization default 0.92, kv_cache_memory_bytes overrides utilization, mamba_block_size must be a multiple of 8 for causal_conv1d, mamba_cache_mode 'align' caches Mamba state only at block-aligned step ends, num_gpu_blocks_override 'Used for testing preemption.'
does_not_prove: Docstrings give no data justifying 16, 0.92, or the align granularity.
bearing: supports: knobs with unjustified defaults (block_size 16, gpu_memory_utilization 0.92, mamba align granularity)

title: Automatic Prefix Caching (vLLM design doc)
quote: the freed blocks are added to the tail of the free queue in the reverse order.
proves: Free-block queue is LRU with eviction from head; a finished request's blocks are freed in reverse so its last block (hashing more tokens, judged less reusable) is evicted first; only full blocks are cached, so a partial final block never hits.
does_not_prove: No measurement backs the reverse-order rule or the full-block-only rule; doc calls prefix caching 'almost a free lunch' without figures.
bearing: supports: free-block ordering and partial-block caching as unmeasured design choices

title: Optimization and Tuning (vLLM docs)
quote: In vLLM V1, the default preemption mode is `RECOMPUTE` rather than `SWAP`
proves: V1 defaults to recompute because 'recomputation has lower overhead in the V1 architecture'; advice under preemption is raise gpu_memory_utilization or lower max_num_seqs / max_num_batched_tokens.
does_not_prove: No benchmark is given for the 'lower overhead' claim.
bearing: supports: re-measuring recompute vs swap (claim unbacked by data)

title: vLLM V1 User Guide
quote: vLLM V1 no longer requires KV cache swapping to handle request preemptions.
proves: GPU<>CPU KV cache swapping is marked Removed in V1; preemption is recompute only.
does_not_prove: Gives no data on the cost of removal; does not discuss interaction with prefix cache or KV offload connectors that now move blocks to CPU anyway.
bearing: supports: swap-on-unified-memory or offload-assisted preemption as open idea

title: vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py (main)
quote: preempted_req = self.running[-1]
proves: Victim selection: FCFS policy preempts the last request in the running list (most recently admitted); PRIORITY policy preempts max (priority, arrival_time). _preempt_request frees the request's blocks, sets num_computed_tokens = 0 and prepends it to the waiting queue; freed blocks go to the prefix-cache free queue, so the recompute can hit its own cached blocks if not yet evicted.
does_not_prove: Code shows mechanism, not why LIFO victim choice was picked; no victim-selection policy based on KV size, progress, or re-hit probability.
bearing: supports: victim selection by KV size/prefix re-hit likelihood (unexplored in vLLM)

title: KV-Cache Layout in FlashInfer
quote: we don’t observe significant performance difference between these two layouts on fp16
proves: NHD vs HND: no significant difference for fp16 KV; HND friendlier for low-precision (fp8) KV; NHD default for readability. Page table treated as block-sparse matrix in CSR form; page_size is tokens per page.
does_not_prove: No numbers published; CUDA only; says nothing about 4-bit/quantized KV or Metal kernels.
bearing: threatens: NHD vs HND as a fp16 research question; supports: layout under low-precision KV / Metal

title: [RFC]: KV cache layout combining all layers per block (#27742)
quote: This will reduce the number of fragments to copy by a factor of num_layers.
proves: Per-layer layout splits each block's KV into num_layers non-contiguous segments; cross-layer per-block layout made transfer 4x faster on Llama-3.1-8B with NIXL/Offloading connectors and 'no noticeable degradation' in model execution; implemented for uniform models in PR #27743; hybrid models with non-uniform page sizes block the change.
does_not_prove: Execution-time claim backed by a private spreadsheet; no attention-kernel study across layouts; hybrid case unresolved; RFC closed as not planned.
bearing: threatens: cross-layer layout for transfers on CUDA; supports: layout x hybrid models gap

title: Inside vLLM's New KV Offloading Connector
quote: DMA performs well, but only for larger block sizes.
proves: Contiguous layout raised physical block size by 2*num_layers (to about 0.5-2 MB from a few KB) and offload throughput ~10x; at 2 MB DMA 83.4 GB/s vs custom kernel 68.5 GB/s; up to 4x lower TTFT and 5x throughput on H100 Llama-3.1-8B.
does_not_prove: PCIe discrete GPU; on unified memory there is no copy engine transfer to optimize.
bearing: threatens: offload transfer-layout ideas on CUDA

title: Tiered KV Cache Offloading in vLLM
quote: each page stores one block of one layer, with all KV heads from across TP ranks gathered into a single contiguous region.
proves: Canonical host layout is per-layer per-block; blocks_per_chunk makes larger I/Os; storage tier more than doubles throughput past ~128 concurrent conversations on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, 2xH100.
does_not_prove: No unified-memory discussion; no TTFT numbers on the page.
bearing: context: offload is now a tier, not preemption

title: flash_attn backend (vLLM API docs)
quote: shape = [num_blocks, num_kv_heads, block_size, 2 * head_size]
proves: FlashAttention backend accepts kernel block sizes that are MultipleOf(16) by default (MultipleOf(64) on XPU, fixed sizes on some FP8/FA4 paths).
does_not_prove: Page truncated; NaN note for fp32 Mamba (blocks 16/32/64) seen only in search snippet.
bearing: context: kernel constrains block-size sweep range

title: vToken: Token-Level Virtualization for Reclaimable KV Caches
quote: Both workloads achieve the best throughput and lowest p95 latency at block size 32
proves: On vLLM v0.18.0, H100 80GB, H2O eviction on LongBench and ShareGPT: block 32 best, block 48 reduces retained capacity but degrades performance; 16 used as minimum. Token-level reclamation cuts retained blocks 27.2%-72.3%, up to 1.37x SLA throughput.
does_not_prove: Sweep is inside a token-eviction setting, two workloads, numbers only in a figure; not a general block-size study.
bearing: supports: block-size tradeoff gap (only sweep found is incidental)

title: When Fancy Eviction Fails: Rethinking Cache Replacement For LLM Prefix Reuse
quote: sophisticated policies designed for traditional caches provide little benefit over LRU
proves: 14 eviction algorithms on traces from two companies, HBM-constrained and large-pool settings: little gain over LRU because session pacing makes recency predictive.
does_not_prove: Concerns eviction policy, not block size or free-block ordering within LRU.
bearing: threatens: fancy prefix eviction policy; supports: keep LRU and vary other knobs

title: Marconi: Prefix Caching for the Era of Hybrid LLMs
quote: precludes rolling back cache entries for partial sequence overlaps
proves: Recurrent (Mamba) state updated in place forces exact-match prefix hits; reuse- and FLOP-per-byte-aware admission/eviction gives up to 34.4x higher token hit rate (71.1% or 617 ms lower TTFT).
does_not_prove: Predates vLLM's align-mode Mamba prefix caching; does not study checkpoint interval (block size) choice on the hit rate vs memory curve.
bearing: threatens: hybrid prefix eviction; supports: Mamba checkpoint granularity (mamba_block_size) study

title: FastSwitch: Optimizing Context Switching Efficiency in Fairness-aware Large Language Model Serving
quote: leads to discontinuity and insufficient granularity in the KV cache memory
proves: Block-based KV causes poor I/O utilization during preemption-induced swaps; FastSwitch gives 1.4-11.2x tail TTFT/TBT speedups over vLLM.
does_not_prove: Built on swap-capable vLLM v0; discrete GPU PCIe.
bearing: threatens: swap-granularity optimizations on CUDA

title: ConServe: Fine-Grained GPU Harvesting for LLM Online and Offline Co-Serving
quote: incremental KV cache management that enables preempting and resuming offline requests at near-zero cost
proves: Sub-iteration layer-wise preemption plus incremental KV management; 2.2x throughput and 2.9x lower online tail latency on Llama-3.1/Qwen-2.5.
does_not_prove: Co-serving of online and offline jobs; not a general preemption policy study.
bearing: threatens: cheap preemption via incremental KV backup

title: Mitigating KV Cache Competition to Enhance User Experience in LLM Inference
quote: it selects the shortest-latency strategy between swapping and recomputation for preemptions
proves: CacheOPT chooses swap or recompute per preemption by predicted latency; up to 3.29x/2.83x lower tail TBT/TTFT.
does_not_prove: One component among five; abstract does not isolate the swap/recompute selector's contribution.
bearing: threatens: per-request swap-vs-recompute selector

title: Towards Multi-Model LLM Schedulers: Empirical Insights into Offloading and Preemption
quote: preemption incurs substantial overhead, largely dominated by model state reload rather than key-value cache transfer
proves: Offloading causes strongly non-linear, model-dependent decode degradation, sharper for smaller models; preemption cost varies across models and hardware.
does_not_prove: Model-level preemption (multi-model), not request-level KV preemption.
bearing: context: measurement study on offload/preemption

title: No Buffer, No Bottleneck: Efficient Zero-Copy KV Cache Offloading for Long-Context LLMs (DirectKV)
quote: naïve zero-copy can be over 20× slower on PCIe and still 2× slower on NVLink-C2C
proves: On GH200, kernels read CPU-resident KV directly with SMEM tiling, no HBM staging buffer: up to 50% less CPU-GPU transfer, 43% less GPU memory, up to 1.2x end-to-end.
does_not_prove: GH200 has distinct HBM and LPDDR tiers; does not apply to fully unified single-pool memory (Apple, MI300A).
bearing: threatens: zero-copy KV on Grace Hopper; supports: unified-memory 'offload' differs

title: Accelerate Large-Scale LLM Inference and KV Cache Offload with CPU-GPU Memory Sharing
quote: NVLink-C2C memory coherency creates a single unified memory address space shared by both the CPU and the GPU.
proves: GH200: 900 GB/s coherent C2C, 96 GB HBM plus 480 GB LPDDR; RMM managed memory lets workloads exceed GPU memory without manual transfers.
does_not_prove: No KV-specific benchmark; internal inconsistency on GPU memory (96 vs 144 GB).
bearing: context: GH200 unified address space

title: The Hitchhiker's Guide to Programming and Optimizing Cache Coherent Heterogeneous Systems: CXL, NVLink-C2C, and AMD Infinity Fabric
quote: the GH200 achieving nearly 16 times higher throughput than H100_CXL and 6 times higher than H100_DIMM at comparable offload sizes
proves: vLLM with weight offload: throughput peaks at an offload size that balances KV capacity against transfer (H100 at 90 GiB, GH200 ~70 GiB); memcpy >99% of time; measured C2C 419 GB/s CPU->GPU, 371 GB/s GPU->CPU.
does_not_prove: Offloads weights, not KV; KV size fixed at 30 GiB in one test; MI300A not evaluated for LLMs.
bearing: supports: KV pool sizing vs other memory as tradeoff on unified hardware

title: MI300A - Exploring the APU advantage (ROCm blog)
quote: All data resides in the HBM memory and is directly accessible to the GPU (XCD) and the CPU (CCD) cores.
proves: MI300A shares one HBM pool; physical page migration is 'neither needed nor useful' but XNACK still handles page faults; hipMalloc vs malloc vs managed allocations differ in first placement.
does_not_prove: No LLM or KV measurement; no allocator or page-size performance numbers. No MI300A KV-cache study found.
bearing: supports: unified-memory KV allocator study (gap)

title: Announcing vllm-metal: Concurrent Serving on Apple Silicon
quote: allocating the remaining budget to a fixed KV cache
proves: vllm-metal sizes a fixed paged KV pool after warmup from --gpu-memory-utilization (default 0.92), caps MLX's buffer cache, uses a paged varlen Metal kernel ported from vLLM's Triton kernel; requests that do not fit wait for pages; SSD-backed offload on roadmap.
does_not_prove: No block size, no preemption behavior, no KV memory measurements; benchmark measures batching not KV management.
bearing: supports: KV pool sizing on 16 GB unified memory (0.92 default unjustified)

title: vllm-metal docs/configuration.md (KV Cache Memory Settings)
quote: `--gpu-memory-utilization` therefore bounds cache capacity rather than admission
proves: On Apple unified memory the KV pool is lazily committed (no zero fill for uniform attention caches), is not wired by mx.set_wired_limit, and can be compressed or swapped by macOS; a startup probe touches min(capacity, 512 MiB) and reads vm_stat Compressions/Swapouts, shrinking the pool if paging occurs, with reserve max(1 GiB, 1/16 of recommended working set). Sliding-window hybrid grouping 'can improve long-context capacity, but not necessarily generation speed.'
does_not_prove: Describes mechanism; no measured cost of OS compression/swap of KV pages on TPOT or of lazy page faults during long prefill.
bearing: supports: OS-level swap/compression of KV on Apple Silicon as unmeasured preemption substitute

title: vllm-metal docs/kv_offloading.md
quote: A larger pool means a smaller KV cache, not extra memory.
proves: On Metal the host offload pool comes out of the same --gpu-memory-utilization budget; default pool = KV of two max-model-len requests, capped at a quarter of KV budget; refuses sliding-window, MLA and hybrid models; disk tier supported.
does_not_prove: No measurement of the tradeoff between offload pool share and active KV pool on 16 GB machines beyond a note on #1037/#737.
bearing: supports: unified-memory offload-pool split as a sizing knob with thin data

title: vllm-metal docs/gqa-decode.md and tests/test_block_size_translation.py
quote: Kernel block size is the view after hybrid-cache translation: a 1056-token
proves: vllm-metal decouples scheduler block size from kernel block size: large hybrid pages (e.g. 544, 1056 tokens) are translated into kernel subpages of 8/16/32; GQA decode picks 256/512-token partitions.
does_not_prove: No published sweep of scheduler block size vs kernel block size on Metal.
bearing: supports: manager-vs-kernel block size decoupling as testable knob on Apple Silicon

proves: mlx_lm.server wires ~75% of RAM via mx.set_wired_limit and the KV cache can grow until kernel panic; maintainer suspects wired limit and is ambivalent about max-kv-size, suggesting disk offload of prompt caches instead.
